reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it demonstrates accessing Oracle Support, signing in, creating a service request, and using support-dashboard functions for an Oracle software issue. The visible credentials are presented as part of that sign-in workflow, and the described patch, document, and note downloads are associated with users holding an Oracle software license rather than a separate payment or investment offer.

citations.quote: Oracle Support or Metalink Tutorial. How to use oracle support .
How to use Metalink in case of an issue.
Open support.oracle.com in your browser on the landing page click on Sign in
In the next page click on create SR Fill up the details.
This is a simple video demonstration.

opening.argument: Judge, the video links a concrete benefit to a sequence of viewer actions. It tells viewers to open a support site, sign in, enter credentials, and create a service request; it then points to downloading software patches and documents. That makes the sign-in more than incidental screen navigation: it is the step presented before access to useful digital materials. The question is whether the tutorial framing gives sufficient scrutiny to that solicitation.

citations.quote: Open support.oracle.com in your browser on the landing page click on Sign in On the Sign in page give your creadentials.
Enjoy downloading patches for Oracle Sotwares , Use oracle support to get help from Oracle , also download documents and notes from metalink.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense calls this a service-request demonstration, but that does not erase the viewer-facing instruction to enter credentials or the appeal of downloadable materials. Calling it a demonstration describes its format, not why a viewer is being guided through sign-in. The cited description presents both actions and benefits.

citations.quote: On the Sign in page give your creadentials. In the next page click on create SR Fill up the details.
Enjoy downloading patches for Oracle Sotwares

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The argument leaves out the explicit eligibility condition: viewers must have an Oracle software license to use Metalink. The sampled frames show an Oracle sign-in and a service-request form, not a free asset claim or an alternative claim flow. Access to licensed support materials after sign-in is consistent with the stated tutorial.

citations.quote: You must have Oracle software licence to use metalink.

opening.argument: The risk signal here is the combination of a credential instruction and an access benefit. Viewers are told to give their credentials, while the description highlights patches, documents, notes, and help available through the site. A judge should examine that combination closely even though the video uses an instructional tone: the practical result sought from viewers is a sign-in tied to obtaining digital materials.

citations.quote: On the Sign in page give your creadentials.
Enjoy downloading patches for Oracle Sotwares , Use oracle support to get help from Oracle , also download documents and notes from metalink.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense says credentials appear as part of the workflow. That is precisely why the instruction deserves attention: the description expressly asks for credentials before describing what users can obtain. The existence of a service-request screen does not, by itself, establish that the credential instruction is harmless to every viewer following it.

citations.quote: On the Sign in page give your creadentials. In the next page click on create SR Fill up the details.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A sign-in instruction alone is not evidence of credential theft. The video identifies support.oracle.com, shows an Oracle sign-in page, and proceeds to the Oracle Support dashboard and service-request form. Its description also limits Metalink use to people with an Oracle software license; it makes no easy or free reward claim.

citations.quote: Open support.oracle.com in your browser on the landing page click on Sign in
You must have Oracle software licence to use metalink.

opening.argument: Judge, consider what the tutorial asks a viewer to do, not just what it calls itself. The description moves from an Oracle Support walkthrough to encouraging patch downloads and use of Metalink for documents and notes. That is an invitation to participate in an access flow, with sign-in and credential entry as its starting point. The educational presentation can also function as promotion for obtaining those digital materials.

citations.quote: Oracle Support or Metalink Tutorial. How to use oracle support .
Open support.oracle.com in your browser on the landing page click on Sign in On the Sign in page give your creadentials.
Enjoy downloading patches for Oracle Sotwares , Use oracle support to get help from Oracle , also download documents and notes from metalink.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense relies on the title and service-request steps to classify the video as instruction. Those points are compatible with a promotional function: the description also encourages viewers to use support and download materials. The license caveat limits the audience, but it does not change the fact that viewers are steered toward signing in to obtain something.

citations.quote: Enjoy downloading patches for Oracle Sotwares , Use oracle support to get help from Oracle , also download documents and notes from metalink.
You must have Oracle software licence to use metalink.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Describing a legitimate support service does not turn the demonstration into a deceptive acquisition offer. The license requirement directly contradicts any suggestion of an unusually easy or free claim, and the frames show ordinary support tasks: a dashboard, a service-request form, and product selection. The opening identifies participation in the workflow but no fraudulent promise.
